newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ households spent less in 1996 than late 80s-SNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ households spent less in 1996 than late 80s-SNZ.

text.p: New Zealand household spending in real terms remains under the level seen in the later 1980s but continued to rise in 1996 out of a trough set in 1994, Statistics New Zealand said on Wednesday.
"The decline has also contributed to New Zealand recording a lower-than-OECD-average rate of increase in consumer spending for the period 1990-96," SNZ said.
Its data showed average household spending was NZ$670.83 a week in 1996, up from 1994's low of $618.76 but still well short of the 1987 level of $729.76.
While spending on health, education and leisure has risen sharply, as well as more being spent on pay television, eating out and computer equipment, spending on clothing and cigarettes has fallen.
Spending on clothing as a proportion of total household spending fell from 5.7 percent in 1986 to 4.4 percent in 1996.
